faq.q: When my XML is malformed, how do I find the error?
faq.a: The tool parses XML with the browser's native DOMParser in application/xml mode. If the document is not well-formed, the status line shows the parser's message and, where the browser provides it, the line and column of the fault — so you can jump straight to the unclosed tag or stray character. Validate does this check without producing formatted output.

faq.q: Can it handle large files, and convert XML to YAML directly?
faq.a: Yes. Files up to 100 MB are accepted (phones are asked to confirm above 25 MB). Large text is kept in memory and only the first 200 KB is shown in the box; Copy and Download give the full result. YAML work runs in a background worker, and large XML is formatted in slices with a progress bar and a Cancel button, so the page keeps responding. In testing on a desktop, a 41 MB XML file formatted in about 14 seconds and a 33 MB YAML file in about 40 seconds. XML → YAML and YAML → XML buttons convert directly, using the same element and attribute mapping as XML ↔ JSON.

faq.q: What parts of an XML document are preserved when formatting?
faq.a: The XML declaration (<?xml …?>), comments, CDATA sections, processing instructions, attributes and namespace prefixes are all kept. Text inside an element marked xml:space="preserve" is left exactly as written, including its internal spaces, while only the whitespace-only gaps between other elements are collapsed and re-indented. Formatting only ever renders into a read-only text box, never into the page, so parsed markup cannot run.

faq.q: Does the YAML side keep my comments?
faq.a: No. YAML is handled by js-yaml 4.1.0, which builds a data model from your document and then re-dumps it; comments are not part of that model, so they are dropped on output. The tool warns you in the status line when your input contained a # comment. Anchors and aliases are resolved, multi-document streams separated by --- are supported, and YAML errors are reported with a line and column.
